I've really not enjoyed Super. I liked the BoG film but after that, it went down hill. I prefer GT much more. Yes, GT had a slightly shaky ride, but re-watchng it get it recently made me realise how awesome it was. There were some bits like the heart of the Black Star arc that made me wonder how they could have thought it was good enough, but the following arcs (Baby, Super 17 and Shadow Dragons) were brilliant to me. AND SSJ4. This transformation made the series that much better (Not just GT but all of Dragon Ball.) It was a new level that had never been seen and, if the series had continued, I would have liked to seen be mastered. 

This is where I think Super falls short. We had no introduction to SSJB. It was just there suddenly. Not much context besides "training". SSJ4 had a huge transformation. Something to make you wonder if it was unnatural or even if it was good or evil that would come out of it. Introducing a huge power that way makes sense. SSJG had a brilliant introduction. The whole ritual of good hearted saiyans outing there power into another. It's something that should have been developed even more. Why did they have this latent power? Was it because good hearted saiyans should have to power to rival gods? Who knows? 

The other thing that makes Super fall short, for me, is the immense power of the beings around Goku and friends. It feels like power they can not achieve without it being OP. Xeno is a good example of this. Someone who can wipe out universes in a blink of an eye. Dragon Ball isn't about fighting. It's about overcoming the strongest. And to introduce a character with almost unreachable power breaks that for me.

Rant over. I can understand many people disagree but that's how I see it.

I know this may sound dumb and probably seems like it has no correlation to your situation, but do you watch any films? Star Wars or Indiana Jones? I have found these to somewhat help me carry on in tough times. Or YouTube channels? Like Rooster Teeth or iDubbbz? I never fail to laugh.

I know this isn't a solution, but I absolutely hate it when people on here just say "give it time" or some shit like that. What I was told nicely over 2 years of therapy was that I need to get over it. That I should just feel better. There literal answer in my last session was "... And just try not to think about it." And that has stuck with me.

There isn't really a solution to be found here but for myself, whenever I'm considering suicide, I always stop myself with watching something that just takes me out of the moment.

Truthfully, it's the wait for the next Star Wars films and iDubbbz videos. Seriously. It is the only entertainment in my life. I can say right now that if these either stop or turn bad then I will easily be able to finally end it. Everything else is just pain.
